newsitem.title: USA: Sallie Mae holders to vote on going private.
newsitem.headline: Sallie Mae holders to vote on going private.

text.p: The Student Loan Marketing Association, better known as Sallie Mae, said Friday its board had approved a plan to restructure as a fully private, federally chartered corporation.
It said the plan will be submitted to a shareholder vote at a special meeting on May 15.
The privatization of Sallie Mae, the nation's largest source of college-education financing, was approved by Congress and signed into law by President Bill Clinton on September 30.
Sallie Mae said the reorganization plan includes an 18-member board of directors, comprised of 10 members who have either served or are serving as directors and eight new nominees.
The new nominees are led by Lawrence Hough, the institution's president and chief executive officer.
The other seven are executives from the private sector, including Peter Ueberroth, former commissioner of baseball and managing director at Los Angeles-based Contrarian Group.

Upon shareholder approval of the reorganization, Sallie Mae will become a state-chartered holding company that will own all a government-sponsored enterprise (GSE) subsidiary. The subsidiary will contain all of Sallie Mae's existing GSE financial assets and other non-GSE subsidiaries.
The GSE subsidiary would be wound down over a 12-year period. Debt obligations of Sallie Mae of the GSE would not be unaffected, Sallie Mae said.
